key_insight: The paper couples XFEM and an optimization-based mixed-dimensional domain decomposition method to solve hybrid-dimensional Biot fracture problems with discontinuous displacement and pressure fields.
engineering_relevance: It enables more realistic and robust simulation of flow-mechanics interactions in fractured porous media, even when fractures cut arbitrarily through the 3D mesh.
method: XFEM on the 3D mesh allows displacement and pressure discontinuities across fractures.
A saddle-point mechanics formulation uses Lagrange multipliers to enforce displacement continuity and recover fracture tractions.
Fixed-stress splitting decouples flow and mechanics, while the mixed-dimensional pressure subproblem is solved with CG.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the combined fixed-stress and CG strategy is highly effective for this class of mixed-dimensional coupled problems.
watch_item: Implementation may be challenging because the method requires stable coupling of nonconforming XFEM discretization, Lagrange multipliers, and mixed-dimensional optimization-based solvers.
paper_title: Hybrid-Dimensional Biot Problem with an Optimization Based Domain Decomposition Approach
